brief.headline: Push faster payment for a 1–2% discount — their 2.25x debt load makes cash valuable to them, and we're already at market-fair pricing

priceAsk.summary: Hold price at ₹66.48/KG; if they push back on faster payment, tie any discount to volume commitment
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹66.48/KG, which sits in the market-fair band of ₹60–81/kg (typical ₹66–73/kg). No room to cut price when they keep only 2.3% profit and we're already near the middle of the market range.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 30 days to immediate payment (or advance) in exchange for a 1–2% discount
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Frees up ₹1.24 Cr of our cash if we go to immediate terms; alternatively, moving 15 days faster frees ₹61.76 L

brief.financialLeverage: They keep about ₹2.30 of every ₹100 they sell — very thin. They owe ₹238.85 Cr against 2.25x their own cash, so cash is tight for them. We buy ₹15.03 Cr a year, which is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue — a meaningful customer, enough to ask for better terms but not so big we can squeeze price hard without risking their ability to supply us. Their debt load means they'll value faster payment, so trade speed for a small discount rather than pushing price down and squeezing an already-thin margin.

evidence.point: We're a big customer — our spend is a real share of their business
evidence.figure: ₹15.03 Cr annual spend is 1.36% of their ₹1102.11 Cr revenue

evidence.point: They carry heavy debt, making cash flow important to them
Their profit cushion is razor-thin — little room to cut price
Our current price is already market-fair, sitting in the typical band
Faster payment would free up meaningful cash for us
evidence.figure: ₹1.24 Cr freed if we move to immediate payment; ₹61.76 L if 15 days faster

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, ₹2437.35 Cr revenue, health B (68/100) — established dextrose supplier, strong financials, a credible drop-in alternate

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist, ₹842.97 Cr revenue, health C (52/100) — growing dextrose capacity, decent alternative

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller, ₹365.39 Cr revenue, health D (27/100) — makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade), exact form match; weaker financials but technically suitable

risks: Their health score is D (21/100) and debt is 2.25x equity — pushing too hard on price could destabilize a fragile supplier; focus the ask on payment speed, not margin squeeze
We're their best price at ₹66.48/KG and already market-fair — any competitor quote below this should be verified carefully (confirm grade, CoA, delivery) before using as leverage
Faster payment frees our cash but also accelerates our outflow — finance must confirm we can afford ₹1.24 Cr up front before we offer it
If they refuse faster payment, we have no price gap to exploit — the fallback is qualifying Gulshan or Sanstar as a second source to create competition next cycle
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to immediate payment on this ₹15 crore account — that's real cash flow for you — and in return we're looking for a 1–2% price reduction to make it work for both sides.
